agent_role: Insolvency Engineer — find ways to leave the protocol with bad debt while extracting good assets

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-DP-03: Reentrant fee collection during _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers — _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) clears SWAP_GUARD_FLAG, allowing collectHookFeesByHook to fall through to direct _transferHookFeesByHook during token callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CEI pattern prevents double-spend: tokensOwed[hookFeeKey] is decremented BEFORE safeTransfer at AMMModule.sol:3128. Second transfer attempt underflows.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-TS-02: Direct swap afterSwap-only pricing bounds DoS — if token has afterSwap=ON/beforeSwap=OFF, DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT reads 0, causing computeRatioX96 to return MIN/MAX_SQRT_RATIO and violate bounds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Self-inflicted config error: admin independently controls beforeSwap/afterSwap flags. HOOK-001 variant. No attacker profit path — admin configures own token.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-01: Dust frontrunning in FixedPoolType — _accumulateDustToWithdrawal gives all accumulated dust to first LP to withdraw
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Dust is 1 wei per swap (rounding). Even 1000 swaps = 1000 wei. Gas costs far exceed extractable value. No material economic impact.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-04: SingleProvider hook price manipulation — malicious hook returns extreme sqrtPriceX96 to extract value from LP
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: By-design trust model: LP sets their own hook at pool creation. Only a compromised hook can manipulate prices. Protocol correctly delegates pricing to hook.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-05: Empty pool price manipulation via snapPrice — attacker front-runs liquidity removal to snap price to extreme value
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Standard Uniswap v3 behavior for empty pool repricing. Requires liquidity==0 and no initialized ticks between current/target. No tokens created/destroyed. Next participant voluntarily interacts at new price.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-07: 100% fee asymmetry — swapByInput allows MAX_BPS fee, swapByOutput rejects it, creating one-directional trap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Intentional design choice consistent across all 3 pool types (DynamicPoolType, FixedPoolType, SingleProviderPoolType). Not a bug.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-08: Off-by-one amountIn in FixedHelper swap-by-output — +1 tolerance at line 1680 could compound across swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Core's balance check at AMMModule.sol:2208 verifies actual token balance per-swap. Any discrepancy triggers revert. Cannot compound because each swap has independent balance check. Confirmed with 100-swap Forge test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CP-10: SingleProvider swapByInput fallback rate arbitrage — when amountOut > reserveOut, fallback to swapByOutput may yield different effective rate
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Rate difference is 1 wei rounding (calculateFixedOutput rounds UP vs calculateFixedInput rounds DOWN). Not economically significant.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CH-04: CLOB gross vs net amountIn mismatch — handler may receive different amount than what Core's balance check expects
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: For input swaps, line 2160 sets swapCache.amountIn = adjustedAmountSpecified (full gross amount). Handler receives and transfers full gross. Balance check uses same gross value. Consistent.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CH-07: Non-token hook fee key asymmetry — _storeNonTokenHookFees uses hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFor)) while withdrawal uses hash(hook, hash(tokenFor, tokenFee))
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: API design convention: for non-token hooks, tokenFee MUST equal tokenFor. This is by-design — hook developers must match convention. Not a vulnerability for correct usage.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CH-08: afterSwapRefund reentrancy into CLOB — afterSwapRefund has NO nonReentrant modifier, allowing executor to call CLOB functions during WETH refund callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB tracks balances per-maker via makerTokenBalance[token][msg.sender]. Executor can only withdraw their OWN deposited tokens, not other makers'. No cross-user fund extraction possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-CH-11: PermitTransferHandler fill-or-kill amount check with hook fees — amountSpecified vs amountIn/amountOut mismatch when hook fees reduce amounts
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: For input swaps: handler receives adjustedAmountSpecified = original amountSpecified (line 2160 override). For output swaps: handler receives adjustedAmountSpecified as amountOut. Both match the fill-or-kill check.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HH-01: CLOB pricing bounds bypass via rounding divergence — CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput rounds up twice while SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96 uses integer sqrt
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Rounding divergence is ~1 unit at Q64.96 scale. For any practical pricing bounds margin, this divergence is sub-wei economically. Not exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HH-05: validateHandlerOrder inverted price bounds — price convention may flip when CLOB order direction reverses
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: amount0/amount1 assignment at lines 212-214 always maps to AMM convention (lower address = amount0). sqrtPriceX96 = sqrt(token1/token0) is consistent regardless of order direction. Admin sets bounds knowing this convention.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HH-08: Direct swap no bounds check with beforeSwap-only config — beforeSwap stores amount but afterSwap never validates
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known HOOK-001 variant. Self-inflicted config error — admin controls beforeSwap/afterSwap flags independently. No attacker profit path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-E02: Flash loan profit — flash loan → add liquidity → swap → remove liquidity → repay with profit
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Swap fees consumed by attacker. After round-trip: endBalance <= startBalance. Confirmed with Forge test and fuzz.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-S01: Token balance solvency — reserves exceed actual token balances after multiple operations
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: balance >= reserve + feeBalance holds after 20+ random swaps. Confirmed with multiple Forge tests.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-S02: Value creation — user profits in both tokens after round-trip swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Cannot gain both tokens after round-trip. Fees ensure net loss. Confirmed with fuzz test (25 runs).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-H05: Reentrancy guard bypass — ERC-777 callback during queued fee transfer bypasses reentrancy guard
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ENTERED bit preserved by _setReentrancyFlags. Reentrant singleSwap/addLiquidity/removeLiquidity all blocked. Confirmed with MaliciousReentrantToken test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: INV-H03: Transient storage hygiene — second swap in same TX reads stale transient data from first swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Each swap writes its own data to transient slots. Second swap overwrites first's data. No stale data leak. Confirmed with Forge test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C21: Callback state corruption (Bunni/Curve pattern) — MaliciousToken re-enters during transfer to read inconsistent mid-finalization state
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMM updates reserves BEFORE token transfer (CEI pattern). View calls during callback see fully-updated state. State-changing re-entries blocked by reentrancy guard.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C25: Fee-on-transfer token phantom liquidity (PancakeSwap pattern) — pool credits more than actually received
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule._collectToken at line 2913-2920 enforces strict balance check: if (balanceAfter != balanceBefore + amount) revert. Fee-on-transfer tokens always fail this and revert. By-design protection.

theft_theses.thesis: Flash loan → add liquidity → manipulate fees → collect inflated fees → remove liquidity → repay with profit
Reentrant fee collection during queued hook fee transfers to double-spend hook fees
Empty pool price manipulation via snapPrice to extract value from subsequent swappers
Off-by-one amountIn in FixedHelper compounding across many swaps to create phantom reserves
afterSwapRefund reentrancy into CLOB to drain other makers' deposited tokens
Fee-on-transfer token creates phantom liquidity that can be drained on removal
Truncation harvesting via 100+ tiny swaps in zero-liquidity edge case
CLOB handler gross/net amountIn mismatch to extract excess tokens from AMM
Fill-or-kill permit mismatch with hook fees to execute swaps at favorable rates
CLOB pricing bounds bypass via rounding to execute orders outside allowed price range
SingleProvider swapByInput fallback rate arbitrage when output exceeds reserves
